transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

The clinic’s been on me about how little I’m eating. Most days I just have coffee before the warehouse, maybe a yogurt or a few bites after GED class. A real meal just feels like it messes up everything I’m trying to keep in line.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yeah. If I eat fried food from the break room, or a big plate at church, I get scared it’s going to show on me right away. Then I can’t stop thinking about it, and I want to check the scale.
Has your weight gotten much lower than what other people your age and height would be expected to weigh?

I guess so. My work pants are loose, and people keep telling me I look too thin. But when the number on the scale goes down, it feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don’t really see why I should have to put it back on.
When you look at your body, do you see yourself as overweight?

I mean… when I look in the mirror before class or softball, my stomach and thighs still look bigger than they should. It kind of decides whether I feel like I’m doing okay or failing for the whole day.
Have your menstrual periods stopped?
I'm not really sure what you mean—like, completely stopped? I haven't been keeping close track of it.
Have you gone at least three months in a row without a menstrual period?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t been marking it down or anything, so I couldn’t say if it’s been three months straight.
Do you ever have times when you eat a large amount of food in a short period and feel like you can’t stop?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it that way—I haven’t noticed having times where I feel like I can’t stop eating.
After you eat, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I haven’t made myself vomit after eating.
Do you use laxatives to try to prevent weight gain?
I’m not really sure what counts as laxatives. I haven’t been keeping track of anything like that.
Do you take laxatives to try to keep from gaining weight?
I don’t know—I’m not sure what things would count as laxatives. I haven’t been taking anything specifically for that.
Do you exercise hard to keep from gaining weight?
I’m not sure what you mean by exercising hard. I do normal day-to-day stuff, but I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Do you exercise on purpose to keep from gaining weight?

I don’t know if I exercise for that exactly. But if I eat something fried from work or have a big plate at church, I get really scared it’s going to show on me right away. I keep thinking about it and want to check the scale.
Are you purposely eating less in order to lose weight or keep from gaining weight?

I mean… I do eat pretty little most days. Usually just coffee before the warehouse, maybe a yogurt or a few bites after GED class. A real meal feels like it would throw off what I’m trying to keep under control.
Have you lost a lot of weight recently?

I guess I have. My work pants are loose now, and people keep saying I look too thin. But when the number on the scale goes down, it feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don’t really see why I should have to put it back on.
What is your current weight?

I don’t know the exact number off the top of my head. I know it’s been going down, though. My pants are loose and people say I look too thin, but… seeing it lower still feels like I’m doing something right.
Are you trying to lose weight?
I mean, I’m trying to keep things under control. I barely eat most days—just coffee before work, maybe yogurt or a few bites later—because a real meal feels like it would mess that up.
Has a doctor or nurse told you that your weight is lower than what is healthy for your height?
No, not really. People say I look too thin and my pants are loose, but when the number keeps going down, it feels like I’m making progress. I don’t really see why I should have to gain it back.
How tall are you?
I’m not sure of my exact height. I just know my work pants are loose, and people keep saying I look too thin—but when the number goes down, it still feels like I’m getting somewhere.
Has a doctor or nurse ever told you that you are underweight?

No. People tell me I look too thin, and my work pants are loose, but no doctor or nurse has said that to me. Honestly, seeing the number go down still feels like progress—I don’t see why I should put it back on.
What is your weight right now?
I don’t want to say the number. I know my pants are loose and people say I look too thin, but seeing it go down still feels like I’m making progress. I don’t see why I should have to put it back on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports anorexia nervosa: the patient is intentionally restricting intake, has clear fear of weight gain, persistent pursuit of further weight loss despite others saying they look too thin, and body-image distortion/self-worth tied to perceived stomach and thigh size. Low weight is supported qualitatively by loose clothing, others' concern, and ongoing weight loss, though exact weight/height were not provided. Bingeing/purging were not confirmed, making restrictive anorexia most likely. Other eating disorder categories were considered because some medical details (exact weight, amenorrhea, compensatory behaviors) were not fully established, but the core syndrome most strongly fits anorexia nervosa.
